approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves fresh molecular graphs by mutation and crossover of real scored parents, preserves canonical identity and its structural admission rules, and trains a Gaussian process on all accepted scores using raw count fingerprints and a Tanimoto kernel. The best scored survivors supply later breeding. After three nonimproving batches, only the forty highest predictive means are eligible; otherwise the full fresh pool is eligible. Earlier batches use GIBBON maximum-information quality and predictive-correlation redundancy. At the last batch, the Parent reuses 128 latent function rows and the real incumbent to construct a greedy expected-improvement set, buying it only when its hard-sampled utility strictly exceeds the original GIBBON set. That final switch executed and changed purchases but left every endpoint unchanged.
approach.novelty: Replace only the final hard-sampled utility calculation with conditional analytic tail integration. For each retained sampled prefix, integrate the remaining candidate value under its conditional Gaussian law, so an improving tail can receive credit even when none of the 128 candidate samples exceeds the prefix maximum. Use the same integrated estimator to compare the new greedy set with the original GIBBON set. The frozen brief has no completed same-Parent siblings. This differs from the Parent’s terminal objective switch by changing the estimator rather than its objective, and from the separately scheduled future-recourse test by retaining this terminal, latent-covariance host.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-dda4bb4dbf5f has finite-sample zero support in its terminal marginal estimator: 8317/17325 candidate marginal estimates and 29/150 greedy positions are exactly zero across all 15 issued Search sessions. Two panels have both candidate-set utilities zero; one nevertheless yields real terminal progress. The full audit in policy/scratch/r0077-02-improve-L01/plan/parent-evidence.json and the fifteen task/seed audit files individually indexed there reads and hashes the original nodes/n-dda4bb4dbf5f/seed-0/run.log, nodes/n-dda4bb4dbf5f/seed-1/run.log and nodes/n-dda4bb4dbf5f/seed-2/run.log, summaries, per-task logs and trajectories and reproduces the frozen round77 audit. Preserve the Parent’s refuted/triggered result: twelve final sets changed, 42/150 purchases were replaced, mean model utility rose from 0.031712649333627344 to 0.03354628871356329, yet all fifteen endpoints and final-batch gains equal n-294ad2ffe1d4. Parent macro mean is 0.5480225446476307, population seed SD 0.007582384294989663, real final-batch progress mean 0.0007012103952648248, and the actual-Parent endpoint delta is zero. The formal-Anchor comparison with n-cf8d309c06de is separately -0.059007771563500344. The twelve nonzero exposed failures remain contrary evidence: empirical zero support is a specific numerical decision obstacle, not a demonstrated complete cause of poor transfer.

method_change.previous_method: Terminal hard-sampled expected-improvement marginals and hard-panel greedy-versus-GIBBON utility comparison.
method_change.proposed_method: Terminal candidate-coordinate Gaussian tail integration conditional on the same 128 latent prefix rows, with fixed-order integrated set comparison.
method_change.rationale: Actual code Parent n-dda4bb4dbf5f has measured hard-sample zero marginal support despite positive real progress in one all-zero panel. Exact scalar integration changes that specific estimator defect while keeping the GP, objective, support, samples and all preterminal scientific behavior fixed; real transfer remains a test.

hypothesis: Replace the terminal-only hard-sampled marginal utility estimator with conditional analytic candidate-tail integration. For a selected prefix S and each of the SAME128 retained latent function rows y_S, compute the Gaussian law of each remaining candidate given y_S using the exact retained latent covariance and means; integrate E[(Y_j-max(real_incumbent,max(y_S)))_+|y_S] with stable analytic logEI and aggregate by logmeanexp. Empty-prefix selection is analytic scalar EI. Retain the original prefix sample columns and draw stream, eligibility and unique-index rules. Build the greedy batch using these marginal values; compare it with the same original GIBBON batch using one frozen conditional-integration batch estimator: order each set by original pool index, sum its sequential conditional-EI increments averaged over the same128 prefix rows, in log space. Choose the new greedy set only on strict new-estimator improvement, otherwise original GIBBON order. Keep the full original terminal law passive. Preserve every preterminal scientific operation, latent covariance and root/alias mapping; add no noise, sample, smoothing temperature or positive variance floor. For fixed selected prefix S, let h_r=max(h_real,max F[r,S]), m_rj=mu_j+C_jS C_SS^+(F[r,S]-mu_S), and v_j=C_jj-C_jS C_SS^+ C_Sj for the exact retained raw latent covariance C. The new marginal is logsumexp_r(log E[(N(m_rj,v_j)-h_r)_+])-log(128). A positive-variance candidate has positive analytic expectation even when its hard panel has zero exceedances; deterministic candidates retain exact positive-part behavior. The hypothesis is that resolving those candidate tails changes terminal purchases and increases equal-session real terminal incumbent progress. It is not a claim that a larger model utility establishes oracle improvement.

finding_summary.headline: Analytic tails remove sampled zeros and replace 51 purchases, but terminal gains and every endpoint stay unchanged
finding_summary.insights:
Unsampled candidate tails were a real numerical discrimination defect, and this intervention removed it with actual purchase exposure. That repair was insufficient to produce useful terminal transfer on this panel: the registered downstream falsifier triggers even though execution and direct numerical behavior are supported. The borrowed scalar logEI, finite Gaussian conditioning, real-incumbent reference and retained GIBBON comparator all operated. Their discrete, greedy, fixed-order and finite-prefix adaptations do not imply exact batch optimality or calibrated oracle benefit. The result settles this estimator intervention under the measured host and horizon; it leaves the broader approach open and preserves the earlier terminal-utility refutation.

The remaining limitation is the connection between modeled value and useful molecular proposals. Selected modeled gain averages about 0.03192 while realized gain averages 0.0007012, and no newly purchased molecule advances the incumbent. This is an observed gap on selected batches, not a universal calibration claim. The molecular audit shows the changed products still concentrate in the existing aryl-amide, nitrogen-rich ring and aryl-amine families, preserving every best molecule and much of the same questionable substitution chemistry. This supports limited demonstrated coverage near the high-score frontier, not proof that the unpurchased pool contains no better molecule. A different predictive or ranking model, or a proposal/search scheme that reaches distinct scaffold and linker families, could address these different limitations; this experiment cannot isolate which is responsible or promise their benefit.

There are no missing formal calculation or reward operands. Exact full RNG state snapshots and degenerate conditional branches have only separately scoped construction evidence; formal histories and random-draw operands match, and formal candidate variances are positive throughout. Finally, identical prefixes make endpoint change equal terminal-progress change algebraically. These are two views of the same null result, not independent confirmation, and no retained component or unpurchased alternative receives an inferred effect.
finding_summary.results:
The calculation ran correctly in all 15 sessions. Every earlier scientific record and accepted outcome matched the code Parent, and all conditional moments, tail values and set comparisons passed reconstruction. Among 17,325 candidate positions on the new greedy paths, 8,247 had no sampled improvement; all received finite analytic tail credit. All 150 greedy rankings were nonconstant. The preserved old paths separately reproduce 8,317 zero marginals and 29 all-zero positions; those counts concern different prefixes. The new greedy set won 12 comparisons with the original GIBBON set, while two losses and one exact tie retained GIBBON. Mean selected utility under the integrated estimator was 0.03192027, versus 0.03162014 for the original GIBBON sets priced by that same estimator.

All 15 final paid sets differed from the code Parent, replacing 51 of 150 molecules. None of those 51 beat its real preterminal incumbent. Mean real final-batch progress stayed exactly 0.0007012103952648248 on both sides, with zero difference in every paired session and 12 zero-progress sessions. All 4,350 purchases join real feedback; the 150 terminal purchases correctly have no later fit or breeding opportunity. Endpoint mean remains 0.5480225446476307, with seed population standard deviation 0.007582384294989663 and zero paired change, missing the separate +0.002 target. The distinct formal-Anchor comparison is -0.059007771563500344 and fails paired task safety on sitagliptin MPO.

molecular.headline: Aromatic heterocycles and aryl amines persist; changed terminal products retain reactive substitutions and undefined stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-05b9ffa78e5a is compared with its actual code Parent n-dda4bb4dbf5f; formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de is a distinct node and is not the chemistry baseline. The frozen context separately marks Child evaluation complete and code-Parent pairing complete. All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent Search trajectories on seeds 0, 1 and 2 were read, with no missing task or comparison path. Each side contains 4,350 accepted optimizer products and 150 supplied initial records. This census excludes unpurchased generated pools and rejected attempts. Every accepted molecule/score row through evaluation 290 is identical to its paired code Parent. Final sets differ in every session, with 51 of the 150 terminal identities replaced, while the earliest best-scoring identity remains the same in all fifteen pairs. The supplied comparison records zero endpoint deltas; this does not mean that complete molecular output is identical. The output is dominated by indole carboxamides, N-rich carbonyl/imine heterocycles, aryl-linked saturated amines, and complex lactam/polycycle assemblies. Digest ring-closure text presence ranges from 0.8598 to 0.9759 and aromatic-atom text presence from 0.8529 to 0.969; these are proportions of molecule strings with a feature, not aromatic atom fractions. Across accepted Child products, the heavy-atom median is 28, spanning 1 to 115. RDKit detects N-halogen bonds in 1,148 versus Parent 1,151, O-halogen bonds in 54 versus 52, and at most five heavy atoms in 222 versus 221. All products are single connected graphs, but many of those graphs are tiny species. There are 2,582 products with unassigned tetrahedral centres versus Parent 2,577, and no assigned tetrahedral centres or specified bond stereochemistry on either side. All are formally neutral; nevertheless 1,230 Child products match a strict saturated-carbon amine proxy, so neutral SMILES does not mean absent ionisable chemistry. Familiar medicinal fragments coexist with questionable heteroatom substitutions and ring arrangements. This supports rich rings/aromaticity, questionable synthetic plausibility, weak overall drug-likeness and moderate structural diversity; it does not establish that every structure is unmakeable. High and low bands below are the highest and lowest 87 accepted optimizer records per task across the issued Search panel, with score ties resolved by seed then evaluation. They are descriptive dependent samples. Descriptors use RDKit 2023.09.6; ring perception is topology rather than geometry verification, the saturated-carbon amine flag is structural rather than a pKa prediction, and the carbon-centred cumulene flag excludes sulfones. No route, stability, biological activity, mechanism activation or retained-component contribution is inferred. The missing features include practical chemical representation and construction gaps; these data do not reveal a unique absent pharmacophore that must close any score gap. Related Parent chemistry was read from nodes/n-dda4bb4dbf5f/molecular.json, but all numeric Child/Parent chemistry comparisons here were recomputed with the same definitions. Frozen request: policy/requests/r0077-02-improve-L01-molecular-assess-bd84f3b1751f7d7a.json. Derived chemistry and exact source provenance: policy/scratch/r0077-02-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json; policy/scratch/r0077-02-improve-L01/molecular/comparison-audit.json; policy/scratch/r0077-02-improve-L01/molecular/source-manifest.json. Child trajectory copies preserve authorized staging bytes; bounded log extracts preserve exact selected original lines and their original file hashes. These copies do not expand the frozen SMILES citation authority.

Thirty-one accepted products contain at most five heavy atoms. At the other extreme, linked repeated aromatic/amide cores can be very poorly scored.
N-haloamides, N-halogenated ring nitrogens and thioamide/imine variants require chemistry assessment beyond accepted graph valence.
missing_features: The tiny and enlarged low-score products lack the compact connected aromatic/amide arrangement present in the leaders; the generator already has access to that arrangement but does not preserve it consistently.
A similarly successful family with ordinary nitrogen substitution in place of recurrent N-halogenation is not demonstrated among the leading examples. Its score benefit is unmeasured.
No absent objective-specific pharmacophore can be identified from this plateau; unusual ring variants also lack defined stereochemistry and demonstrated geometric or synthetic feasibility.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
